title: "Current Programme"

## Chemically meaningful density fields

My current programme aims to develop a new generation of density-field molecular simulation methods for chemically specific soft matter.

The central idea is that density fields should not be treated only as computational devices. They should become physically interpretable and chemically meaningful variables.

## Main directions

### Fluctuation-aware field formulations

Traditional hybrid particle–field molecular dynamics relies on mean-field approximations. A major goal is to develop formulations that retain the computational advantages of density fields while improving the treatment of fluctuations.

### Physically grounded field functionals

A second direction is to connect field-based interactions with liquid-state theory, equations of state and classical density functional concepts.

### Field-based free-energy and morphology sampling

Many soft-matter systems are governed by changes in morphology: aggregation, adsorption, insertion, phase separation, interfacial restructuring and self-assembly. Density fields provide natural collective variables for describing these processes.

### Applications

Target systems include polymer melts, nanocomposites, soft interfaces, biomembranes and nanoplastics, where mesoscale organization and molecular specificity are both essential.
